summary: STATIC REVIEW ONLY (no cmd.exe/PowerShell runtime on this Linux pod) of the powershell-not-recognized fix. Reviewed /app/windows/create-desktop-shortcuts.bat, create-desktop-shortcuts.ps1 and _env.bat. VERDICT: the fix is CORRECT and will work on a PC whose PATH lacks System32. No blocking bugs found; 2 LOW nits reported. No files modified.

windows_script_static_review.issue: FIX VERIFIED. (1) L3 `call "%~dp0_env.bat"` is present; _env.bat itself uses only cmd internals (set / if exist / for), so it runs even with a broken PATH. (2) L4 sets PS to the absolute %SystemRoot%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe - %SystemRoot% is always defined by Windows, so this resolves regardless of PATH; L5 falls back to bare `powershell`, which _env.bat L19 has just made resolvable by prepending %SystemRoot%\System32;%SystemRoot%;...\Wbem;...\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0 to PATH. (3) L6 quoting is valid cmd syntax: "%PS%" quoted (path has no special chars needing more), -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "%~dp0create-desktop-shortcuts.ps1" - %~dp0 keeps its trailing backslash so the concatenation is correct and space-safe. (4) `if errorlevel 1` on L7 immediately follows the call and is outside any parenthesised block, so no delayed-expansion problem; _env.bat's `exit /b 0` runs BEFORE the call so it cannot pollute errorlevel. If powershell.exe is truly missing, cmd sets errorlevel 9009 (>=1) and the error line prints. All 8 lines are CRLF-terminated.

CORRECT. Arguments = '/c ""<full path to .bat>""'. Per `cmd /?` rule 2, because there are more than two quote characters cmd strips only the leading quote and the last quote, leaving `"C:\...\start-prod.bat"` - i.e. the path stays quoted and works with spaces (e.g. C:\Program Files\...). TargetPath cmd.exe is absolute (%SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe) so the shortcut does not depend on PATH either. WorkingDirectory = $here (windows folder) and all three targets (start-prod.bat, start-dev.bat, stop-erp.bat) exist in /app/windows.

CORRECT. No PS7-only syntax (no ??, ?., ternary, -Parallel). `$icon = if (...) {...} else {...}` (if-as-expression) is PS3+; New-Object -ComObject WScript.Shell, [Environment]::GetFolderPath('Desktop'), Split-Path/Join-Path/Resolve-Path and Write-Host -ForegroundColor are all Windows PowerShell 5.1 safe. $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path is populated when invoked via -File, so $here is right. Join-Path $here '..' + Resolve-Path is valid ($here has no trailing backslash). File is ASCII, no BOM, all lines CRLF.

LOW nit: when desktop\build\icon.ico exists, IconLocation is set to the bare file path with no `,<index>`. WScript.Shell documents the format as "path,index"; safest is `$icoCandidate + ',0'`. Not currently triggered - /app/desktop/build contains only icon.placeholder.txt, so the shell32.dll,15 / ,27 fallbacks (which do include an index) are used.

LOW nit: the message is emitted for ANY non-zero exit, including a genuine COM/shortcut-write failure, and then blames a missing PowerShell install. Consider `if errorlevel 9009 (echo PowerShell not found...) else if errorlevel 1 (echo Shortcut creation failed...)`.

CONFIRMED as requested: PATH is prepended with %SystemRoot%\System32;%SystemRoot%;%SystemRoot%\System32\Wbem;%SystemRoot%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0, so the bare `powershell` fallback resolves. Carried over from iteration_152 and unchanged: start-prod.bat/start-dev.bat netstat regex is still state-agnostic (MEDIUM) and :pick_ip still does not filter virtual adapters (LOW).

Remaining Windows debt: netstat LISTENING-state regex (MEDIUM), LAN IP adapter selection (LOW), plus the pre-existing missing brute-force lockout on POST /api/auth/login.
rca_of_the_issue: Original failure: create-desktop-shortcuts.bat invoked bare `powershell` without calling _env.bat, so on a PC whose PATH lacks C:\Windows\System32 cmd could not resolve the executable ('powershell' is not recognized, errorlevel 9009). The fix removes the PATH dependency entirely by using %SystemRoot%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe and additionally repairs PATH via _env.bat for the fallback.
